title: Topology: See The World Differently
category_reason: Pure topology primer; TDA and physics applications are secondary illustrations, the main subject is topology itself
thesis: Interactive introduction to topology: open sets and continuity, homeomorphism and surface classification (Euler characteristic chi=2-2g), Mobius/Klein bottle non-orientability, fundamental group (pi_1(S^1)=Z, pi_1(torus)=Z x Z), Brouwer fixed-point / hairy-ball / Poincare-Hopf, and topological data analysis as an application.
key_claims: Open sets (not points) are the correct notion of 'near' in topology; continuity is preservation of open sets
Homeomorphism = continuous bijection with continuous inverse; the mug/donut equivalence is the canonical example
Euler characteristic chi = V - E + F is a topological invariant; for closed orientable surfaces chi = 2 - 2g
Classification of closed surfaces: sphere (chi=2), torus (chi=0), connected sums; genus g determines homeomorphism class
The Mobius strip and Klein bottle are non-orientable; a single-sided surface has no consistent 'inside/outside'
The fundamental group pi_1(X, x0) counts homotopy classes of loops; pi_1(S^1) = Z (winding number), pi_1(torus) = Z x Z, pi_1(S^2) = 0
Brouwer fixed-point theorem, hairy-ball theorem, and Poincare-Hopf index theorem link topology to analysis and physics
Persistent homology (TDA) turns point clouds into barcodes of topological features; applications to data science, chemistry, cosmology
visualizations: three.js: surface gallery (sphere, torus, Mobius, Klein)
canvas 2D: loop & winding number on S1
canvas 2D: TDA point cloud & persistence diagram
internal_tensions: TDA is presented as a practical application but the math required (Cech nerve, persistence modules) is only sketched - the reader gets intuition without the algebra
The surface classification theorem is stated and illustrated but the proof (cut-and-paste / triangle decomposition) is not given
The hairy-ball / Poincare-Hopf connection is stated as a fact with a flow visualization but the index-theoretic argument is not developed

title: Deep Neural Networks Entmystifiziert
category_reason: Main subject is deep neural networks and deep learning fundamentals
thesis: German interactive learning game demystifying deep neural networks from a single neuron through activation functions, layer composition, feature hierarchy, training/loss landscape, backprop, representation geometry, depth-vs-width, ResNets, to expert topics (superposition/polysemanticity, lottery tickets, grokking, circuits, scaling laws), presenting the standard deep-learning narrative.
key_claims: A neuron computes a weighted sum + bias + nonlinearity; activation functions (ReLU, sigmoid, tanh) make the network nonlinear and thus expressive
Depth gives an exponential advantage: O(N^L) piecewise-linear regions for L layers vs O(N*L) for a wide shallow net
Deep nets progressively untangle entangled input manifolds - each layer applies a piecewise-linear (ReLU) transformation that simplifies the geometry
Superposition / polysemanticity: many features share neurons; linear probing can extract them; this is why interpretability is hard
Backprop is the chain rule applied to a computation graph; ResNets solve the vanishing-gradient problem via skip connections
Weight matrices of trained nets are smooth in frequency space (low-frequency dominated), which is a signature of generalization
Grokking: a net can memorize a task for many epochs, then abruptly generalize - a phase transition in the loss landscape
Scaling laws: test loss L(N,D) follows a power law L proportional to N^-0.076 in parameters; compute-optimal allocation predicts emergent capabilities
Mechanistic interpretability (circuits): individual features/computations can be isolated; a 'circuit' is a subgraph responsible for a behavior
methods_math: scaling laws (power law in N, D)
visualizations: canvas 2D: activation function plots (ReLU, sigmoid, tanh)
canvas 2D: ResNet gradient flow / skip connections
internal_tensions: Presents the standard DL narrative (depth = good, scaling = good) without engaging with the 'why does it work' open questions; the expert sections gesture at the problems but do not resolve them
Grokking and superposition are presented as settled phenomena, but their theoretical explanations remain speculative
The scaling-law exponent (-0.076) is presented as empirical fact; the theoretical derivation is not given

title: Faserbündel & Fibrationen - Eine interaktive Reise
category_reason: Pure differential geometry / algebraic topology (fiber bundles, fibrations, homotopy); no AI content
thesis: German interactive tour of fiber bundles and fibrations following Sorensen's 'An Introduction to Fiber Bundles and Fibrations': local vs global structure, transition functions and the cocycle condition, vector bundles, the Hopf fibration S1->S3->S2, the homotopy lifting property, the vertical tangent bundle ker Df, and the long exact sequence yielding pi_1(S1)=Z and pi_i(S2) isomorphic to pi_i(S3) for i>2.
key_claims: Local != global: a space can be locally a product (trivial) yet globally twisted (Mobius); the twist is invisible in any single chart
A fiber bundle is a space E -> B where each fiber pi^-1(b) looks like F; transition functions g_ab : U_a cap U_b -> Aut(F) must satisfy the cocycle condition g_ab * g_bc * g_ca = I
Vector bundles (fiber = R^k) are the special case; the Mobius bundle is non-trivial because every section must have a zero (intermediate value theorem)
The Hopf fibration S1 -> S3 -> S2 is the canonical non-trivial bundle; its fibers are linked circles with integer Hopf invariant
A fibration generalizes a bundle by replacing 'local triviality' with the homotopy lifting property (HLP); every continuous map can be replaced by a homotopy-equivalent fibration
The vertical tangent bundle T_f := ker Df consists of directions tangent to the fibers - movement that does not change the base point
The long exact sequence in homotopy for a fibration F -> E -> B connects pi_n(F), pi_n(E), pi_n(B) in a balance equation (exactness: im = ker)
Applying the long exact sequence: pi_1(S1) = Z (via universal cover R -> S1), and pi_i(S2) isomorphic to pi_i(S3) for all i > 2 (via Hopf fibration), so pi_3(S2) = Z - counterintuitively non-zero

The Hopf fibration is visualized in 3D via stereographic projection, but S3 lives in R4; the 4th dimension is hidden, and the linked-fiber structure is shown but not proved
The result pi_3(S2) = Z is presented as 'shocking' but the geometric intuition (why linked fibers force non-trivial maps) is only sketched, not derived

title: Backprop als Funktor - Eine interaktive Reise
category_reason: Main subject is backpropagation and supervised learning, reformulated via category theory; fundamentally about neural network training
thesis: German interactive walkthrough of Fong-Spivak-Tuyeras' 'Backprop as Functor' (arXiv:1711.10455): a learner is a tuple (P, I, U, r) where the request function r is the missing ingredient for composing learning algorithms; learning algorithms form a symmetric monoidal category Learn; gradient descent L_eps,e : Para -> Learn is a faithful, object-injective, strong symmetric monoidal functor; backpropagation is precisely the composition rule in Learn; the full chain NNet -> Para -> Learn shows neural nets are automatically learning algorithms.
key_claims: Two learners A->B and B->C cannot be composed without a backward channel: the front learner has no training pair (a, b') - the request function s : Q x B x C -> B supplies the missing 'desired output'
A learner is a 4-tuple (P, I, U, r): parameter space, implementation, update, and request; the request is trivial for a single learner but essential for composition
Learn is a symmetric monoidal category: objects are sets, morphisms are equivalence classes of learners, composition is series, tensor is parallel, braiding allows wire crossings
Para is the category of differentiable parametrized functions (objects R^n, morphisms (P, I) with I : P x R^n -> R^m differentiable)
Theorem III.2: for any eps>0 and error function e with partial-e/partial-x invertible, gradient descent L_eps,e : Para -> Learn is a faithful, object-injective, strong symmetric monoidal functor
Backpropagation is not a separate algorithm - it is the formula for composition in Learn: U_A = U_B * U_C with the request s_C substituted

NNet is a purely combinatorial category (objects = layer sizes, morphisms = connectivity patterns); I_sigma : NNet -> Para adds activation functions; the chain NNet -> Para -> Learn makes any net a learning algorithm

Bimonoid structure (mu=addition, delta=copy, eta=unit, epsilon=delete) in Learn explains wiring: a neuron is a composite of 5 atoms (lambda, beta, sigma, mu, delta); weight tying follows from the comonoid request rule

The sufficient condition on error functions (partial-e/partial-x invertible) is satisfied by MSE and product loss; cross-entropy is 'almost' an example (singular at 0 and 1); the request has no eps (a coincidence of quadratic loss)
Learn sits between Lens (trivial parameter space) and Open Game (best response) - the request function is the same idea as put/coplay

internal_tensions: The paper's main theorem is proved by a 9-line chain of equations, but the proof relies on the chain rule and the invertibility assumption; the 'why' (what makes gradient descent special among all update rules) is not addressed
The request function r has no eps - the page notes this is a coincidence of quadratic loss, but the conceptual meaning (why the backward channel is 'free') is not explained
Cross-entropy is 'almost' an example but breaks at the boundaries; the practical workaround (staying in (0,1)) is stated but the theoretical gap (no global functor for CE) is left open
The NNet -> Para -> Learn chain is clean but hides the fact that real nets use weight sharing, sparsity, and non-differentiable operations (e.g., max-pooling) that break the framework

title: Die Geometrie der Wahrheit - Interaktiv
category_reason: Main subject is LLM interpretability: finding a linear 'truth direction' in LLM activations and testing it causally
thesis: German interactive walkthrough of Marks & Tegmark's 'The Geometry of Truth' (COLM 2024, arXiv:2310.06824): LLMs represent truth/falsehood of simple factual statements as a linear direction in activation space; the direction is found unsupervised (PCA), generalizes across structurally and topically diverse datasets (transfer), and is causally effective (adding theta to a false statement's activation makes the model output TRUE); the direction emerges with scale (7B->13B->70B).
key_claims: LLMs can output falsehoods while 'knowing' better (hallucination, sycophancy, deliberate deception); the inner state may disagree with the output
A concept (e.g., 'truth') is represented as a direction theta in high-dimensional activation space, not a single neuron; a linear probe is just a dot product theta*x with sign read-off
The key activation is over the sentence-ending punctuation mark (the period), in middle layers (Layer 15 for 13B) - this is where the whole sentence is summarized
PCA (unsupervised, label-free) finds the truth direction as PC1: the direction of maximum variance separates true from false statements

The truth direction generalizes: a probe trained on cities transfers to Spanish vocabulary, number comparisons, etc. (out-of-distribution); training on cities+neg_cities improves transfer (opposites cancel the spurious 'association' feature)

Causal intervention (the strongest evidence): adding theta to a false statement's activation makes the model output TRUE on a dataset the probe never saw; Mass-Mean outperforms LR and CCS in 7/8 conditions
The likely dataset (no truth content, only plausibility) shows truth != plausibility: a plausibility probe is perfect on sp_en_trans (r=0.95) but below chance on negated datasets (r=-0.63, -0.89)

Negation causes axis rotation across layers: cities and neg_cities axes are antipodal in early layers, orthogonal in middle layers, aligned in later layers - explained by two competing features (truth f+ and association f-)
Larger models have more abstract, unified representations: 7B groups by surface features, 13B separates cleanly but sometimes in opposite directions, 70B merges into one common direction

Mass-Mean probing (difference of class means, no optimization) is competitive with logistic regression and CCS for classification, and superior for causal intervention; the inverse-Sigma correction (Fisher LDA) handles correlated features

internal_tensions: The point clouds are explicitly synthetic illustrations (stated in the footer), not real LLaMA activations - the qualitative structures match the paper but the exact numbers are approximate
The paper only tests simple, unambiguous factual statements; it cannot distinguish 'true' from 'generally believed', 'undisputed', or 'verifiable' - the scoping is acknowledged but limits the claim
Only the LLaMA-2 family was studied; whether the truth direction is architecture-specific or universal is open
Mass-Mean's superiority in causal intervention (7/8 conditions) is unexplained - the authors say 'we don't know'; the inverse-Sigma correction helps but does not fully account for the gap
The likely dataset result (plausibility != truth) is strong but relies on the assumption that the likely dataset captures plausibility cleanly; the 100.-most-likely token choice is a heuristic
